issue.title: PhysicalLightingModel: Share common terms between the lighting paths.
issue.body:
Related issue: #35436

**Description**

Every direct light rebuilt terms that do not depend on the light (`dotNV`, the GGX alpha, the Lambert BRDF), and the indirect paths rebuilt the Lambert BRDF and the dielectric scattering scale. They are now built once in `start()`, and `BRDF_GGX()` accepts the half vector and dot products its caller already has. Also: `getDistanceAttenuation()` computes the falloff once, the radiance contexts leave the normalization to `transformDirection()`, and `roughnessToMip()` returns the last mip for a constant roughness of one.

| Fragment WGSL, 5 lights | `dev` | PR | |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `MeshStandardNodeMaterial` | 13,351 chars | 12,198 chars | −8.6% |
| `MeshStandardNodeMaterial`, shadows | 18,644 chars | 17,496 chars | −6.2% |
| `MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial` | 13,669 chars | 12,516 chars | −8.4% |
| `MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial`, all features | 37,483 chars | 36,321 chars | −3.1% |
| `MeshLambertNodeMaterial` | 5,225 chars | 5,145 chars | −1.5% |
| Test scene, all 30 shader modules | 288,548 chars | 277,071 chars | −4.0% |

The output does not change: a WebGPU render of the test scene (Chrome 156, Apple M3 Max, 512 × 512) is pixel-identical to `dev`. The scene has 26 meshes (standard over a roughness × metalness grid, physical with clearcoat, sheen, iridescence and anisotropy, Lambert, Phong, toon), five lights, two shadow maps and an environment map. GPU frame time was not measured.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issue.title: WebGPUAttributeUtils: Avoid subarray allocations when padding attributes.
issue.body:
Related issue: #35436

**Description**

Padding an attribute to a 4-byte stride, or a vec3 storage attribute to vec4, created one `subarray()` view per item, on creation and on every update. The components are now copied through unsigned integer views of the two buffers, so the bytes stay the same as with `TypedArray.set()`.

| 200,000 items | `dev` | PR | |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| vec3 storage attribute, create | 7.9 ms | 1.4 ms | 5.6× |
| vec3 storage attribute, update | 8.8 ms | 2.4 ms | 3.6× |
| Normalized `Uint8` ×3 attribute, create | 7.8 ms | 1.3 ms | 6.2× |
| Normalized `Uint8` ×3 attribute, update | 8.1 ms | 1.5 ms | 5.6× |

Node 24 on an Apple M3 Max, median of 25 runs. The uploaded bytes are identical for 8 attribute layouts, signalling NaNs included.

release.name: repo-3ffff541
release.body:
A script that runs agents by the dozen no longer takes The Office over. If a batch job spawns headless agents (`agy --print`, `claude -p`), each in a temp folder of its own, they used to fill the floor and hide the sessions you opened yourself.

- **Your sessions first:** the floor draws 24 desks. They now go to each room in turn, and to the sessions you opened that are at work or need you before a script's workers. One big room can no longer push every other project into "+N more desks upstairs".
- **No more "(unknown)" room:** a headless Antigravity run is named after the folder it runs in.
- **Finished runs leave:** a headless Antigravity run that has handed in its answer walks out, instead of sitting at its desk for half an hour as "went quiet".
- **One room per script:** workers that each get a throwaway temp folder (`myjob-SB2Np4`, `myjob-m4yheshe`…) share one room named after the folders' prefix.

## Update

```bash
claude plugin marketplace update makio64
claude plugin update theoffice@makio64
```

Then start a new session (or restart Claude Code): a running session keeps the version it loaded.

issue.title: WebGPURenderer: Reduce CPU work in node builds, uniform updates and attribute padding.
issue.body:
Related issue: -

**Description**

Seven small changes to `WebGPURenderer` that came out of profiling a text library on top of it. Each commit stands alone and can be reviewed or dropped separately. The first four change no shader and no behavior. The last three are called out below.

**No shader or behavior change**

- `WebGPUAttributeUtils`: padding an attribute to a 4 byte stride, or a vec3 storage attribute to vec4, created one `subarray()` view per item, on the first upload and on every update. The components are now copied through unsigned integer views, so the bytes are the same as with `TypedArray.set()`, NaN payloads included.
- `UniformsGroup`: every update of an int or uint uniform created a new `Int32Array` or `Uint32Array` view of the buffer. One view per type is kept and dropped with the buffer in `release()` and `clone()`.
- `NodeManager.updateGroup()`: the last seen version of a group was looked up in a `ChainMap` for every shared uniforms group of every render object in every frame. `NodeUniformsGroup` now keeps that version itself. A clone starts without one.
- `NodeBuilder` / `Node`: `hashNodes` is a `Map` and holds only nodes with a custom hash, since a node with the default hash can only find itself. `getCacheKey()` caches the hashes of property names. The per node data has a stable shape and is read once in `getDataFromNode()`. Node properties are iterated without `Object.values()`, and the finished build stages are bits instead of one object per node and stage.

**Shader text changes, same result**

- `ScreenNode`: `setup()` created a new uniform for every build. Shared groups order their members by node id, so that uniform came last, except in a build that also created another member lazily (a camera matrix, for example). The same material then got different WGSL, and another shader module and pipeline, depending on which build ran first. The screen size and viewport uniforms already shared their value; they now share the node.
- `PhysicalLightingModel`: every direct light rebuilt terms that do not depend on the light (`dotNV`, the GGX alpha, the Lambert BRDF), and the indirect paths rebuilt the Lambert BRDF and the dielectric scattering scale. They are now built once in `start()`, next to the terms the model already shares, and `BRDF_GGX()` accepts the half vector and dot products its caller has. `getDistanceAttenuation()` computes the falloff once for both branches, the radiance contexts leave the normalization to `transformDirection()`, and `roughnessToMip()` returns the last mip for a constant roughness of one.

**Behavior change**

- `Renderer`: a transparent double-sided object is split into a back and a front pass so that it blends in order. Shadow passes inherit `transparent` and `side` from the object's material, so each such caster was built and drawn twice per shadow map. A shadow pass writes depth, which does not depend on the draw order, so it is now drawn once. The split stays when `shadowMap.transmitted` is enabled, because transmitted shadows read the color of the pass.

**Measurements**

Apple M3 Max, Node 24.18, no GPU involved. The machine was under load, so these are user CPU times from interleaved runs.

- Node build (`WGSLNodeBuilder.build()` of 21 materials: basic, Lambert, Phong, standard with maps and shadows, physical, toon, instanced, points, sprite, line, two custom TSL materials). With the `NodeBuilder` commit alone the generated WGSL is identical in all 21 cases and the build takes 16.8 % less CPU (35.97 ms to 29.94 ms summed over the cases; a lit standard material 2.40 ms to 2.07 ms, a physical material with every feature 6.41 ms to 5.29 ms). The whole branch measured 16.3 % less in a noisier run.
- Attribute padding, 200,000 items: a vec3 storage attribute 11.3 ms to between 1.5 and 2.1 ms on creation; a normalized `Uint8` x3 attribute 8.3 to 9.7 ms to between 1.4 and 1.5 ms. The uploaded bytes are identical for 8 layouts, signalling NaNs included.
- `ScreenNode`: a material that reads `viewport` and `cameraProjectionMatrixInverse` gets different WGSL for its first build and for a rebuild on `dev`, and the same WGSL on this branch.
- `PhysicalLightingModel`: the fragment shader of a standard material lit by five lights (directional, point, spot, hemisphere, ambient) is 6 to 9 % shorter (13,351 to 12,198 characters); a physical material with every feature 3 % shorter.

`npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run test-unit` (1982 pass, 0 fail, 1 todo) and `npm run test-unit-addons` (147 pass) pass.

Not measured: anything on a GPU. The shadow pass and lighting model changes were checked in the generated WGSL and by reading, and the screenshot tests were not run locally, so I would appreciate a close look at those two and at the CI screenshots.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

The Office now opens in your browser when you use Claude Code in a terminal, as the same pixel art as the desktop app's pane, instead of a text view. `/theoffice` (or a tab's name after it, or **🏢 Open The Office** above the prompt) opens it there, on the tab you picked last. `/theoffice browser` does the same from the desktop app.

- **Live:** the page redraws itself as your agents work. A hand going up shows within about two seconds, and a drawing that hasn't changed is never reloaded.
- **One server:** opening it again reuses the server already running. It listens only on `127.0.0.1` behind a random token, and stops by itself half an hour after its last page closes (or press **Stop server**).

Codex, Cursor, Antigravity and the VS Code extension show the same page in their panels, so they get the new menu and live updates too.

## Update

```bash
claude plugin marketplace update makio64
claude plugin update theoffice@makio64
```

Then start a new session (or restart Claude Code): a running session keeps the version it loaded.

release.body:
Jurilix llama.cpp runtime based on upstream b12144 (69ee2ecc0150ba7d1204a7f7393dfd651569db8c), preserving the Jurilix parser fixes, precompiled Metal shaders and inference optimizations.

Patch SHA-256: bed6dffef6948ddcecc082da5266eaa9496cea48d22083c164d458abb1cc1e38.

macOS arm64 was built and tested natively on Apple M3 Max, with macOS 13.3 minimum. All four parser/grammar suites pass. A finite smoke comparison against b12098 using installed Gemma E4B, all four product LoRAs and MTP produced identical outputs and token counts for five chat requests, restored the cached prompt after adapter switching, and produced bit-identical 768-dimensional embedding vectors. This is smoke coverage, not a full model quality qualification.

Windows CPU and Vulkan were built from the same patched source and passed native static/shared parser suites. CUDA 12.4 uses that verified patched core with the exact official upstream b12144 CUDA plugin and redistributables. A separate audited recipe enforces the core ID, source commit and patch digest before downloading. Native Windows import/symbol resolution, server device discovery, bounded archives and reconstructed file hashes passed in run 42174018431. Jurilix-specific CUDA kernel fusions are not included in this composed variant. The CI runner has no NVIDIA GPU; GPU inference and performance are not qualified. Native CI receipts and component provenance accompany the archives.

Metal stress coverage: 4,748/4,749 FLASH_ATTN_EXT cases and all 240 fa_vec slice cases pass. One 20,000-token case crosses the numerical tolerance (0.000503021 vs 0.0005). A bounded 96-case diagnostic with 24 fixed seeds reproduces identical errors and failing seeds on both b12098 and b12144, including with GQA disabled. This is a pre-existing input-dependent precision limitation; the full stress suite is not all-pass. No tolerance or runtime code was changed to hide the failure. See macos-validation.json and native-test-evidence-macos-arm64.tar.gz.

release.name: user-a86baa18/repo-da3a91bf
release.body:
GPU Performance Agent 2.3.0 comes from running the agent skill end to end on two real WebGPU three.js projects. Its A/B verdicts now explain themselves, it detects when other GPU work skews the timings, and the skill covers the gaps the trials exposed.

```sh
npx skills add Makio64/gpu-perf-agent -g
```

**Highlights**

- **A/B verdicts that explain themselves:** a paired status line now ends with why a row did not decide, e.g. `INCONCLUSIVE — … (-20.4%, 95% CI -4.15..-0.12 ms; paired, 8 rounds, needs CI beyond ±0.52 ms)` or `…, gpu-saturated`. One contended round no longer blocks the whole comparison.
- **GPU contention detection:** GPU timing above 1.2x the frame interval while frames stay on time is marked `contended`. Another browser or profiling agent was sharing the GPU, so the capture is not used as evidence or as a baseline.
- **Accurate pass labels:** passes are named after the steady-state work they time, not after init-time passes like PMREM.
- **`inspect --section rounds`:** per-round values for an A/B, "candidate faster in 7 of 8 rounds", and the median paired delta.
- **Reproducible confirmation:** the printed `ab` command keeps `--chromium-arg`, the ANGLE backend, timeouts and `--headful`.
- **Better agent skill:**
  - capture at the user's device size
  - wait past loaders and intro animations
  - a GPU-share rule for "no bottleneck"
  - `npx gpu-perf-agent@latest` when a project pins an old release
  - what UNVERIFIED and INCONCLUSIVE mean from `ab`
  - handling many cheap post-processing passes

See the [changelog](https://github.com/Makio64/gpu-perf-agent/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for details.

Validation: 457 unit tests passed (66 browser tests skipped in that run); 78 of 78 browser integration tests passed on Chrome 156 / Apple M3 Max.

[Website](https://makio64.github.io/gpu-perf-agent/) · [Full reference](https://github.com/Makio64/gpu-perf-agent/blob/master/docs/reference.md) · [Agent skill](https://github.com/Makio64/gpu-perf-agent/blob/master/skill/SKILL.md)

**Highlights**

- **Automatic per-pass GPU timing** (`timestampWrites` for WebGPU, `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2` for WebGL2) with no app changes. The digest shows GPU busy time per frame and the most expensive passes with their source location.
- **Trustworthy comparisons:** separate captures mark clock-sensitive GPU deltas `UNVERIFIED (screen: better|same|worse)`, and `ab` confirms them with interleaved base/candidate rounds in one browser. A `DIFFERENT-WORK` status catches "speedups" that just draw less.
- **Faster iteration:** a warm background Chrome daemon, `agent --url … --base base.json` to capture and compare in one call, bounded digests and JSON, and lighter tool overhead.
- **Evidence for agents:** `inspect` pulls one section of a saved report (GPU passes, CPU hotspots, errors, samples) instead of loading the whole file; CPU hotspot attribution on CPU-bound pages.
- **MCP:** protocol `2025-11-25`, new `ab_compare_webgpu`, `inspect_webgpu_report` and `doctor_webgpu` tools.
- **Rewritten skill:** a seven-step checklist, a quick start that also works with older releases, tables explaining every digest line and comparison status, troubleshooting for "janky but clean" captures, and a report template. The README now lists each agent's global skill folder, including Antigravity's `~/.gemini/config/skills`.

Fixes since the 2.2.0 preview: MCP `doctor_webgpu` no longer reports WebGPU unavailable on capable machines; warm-daemon failures no longer load the page twice; `--wait-for-hook-timeout` (default 15 s); `--server` forwards the right options; `--preset profile` records its trace; clearer `Trust:` and error lines.

Exit codes: `0` ok / improved / unchanged / unverified / inconclusive, `1` regression or budget failure, `2` invalid or mismatched evidence, `3` CLI or runner error. See the [changelog](https://github.com/Makio64/gpu-perf-agent/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for the full list.

Validation: 442 unit tests passed (66 browser tests skipped in that run); 78 of 78 browser integration tests passed on Chrome 156 / Apple M3 Max.

[Website](https://makio64.github.io/gpu-perf-agent/) · [Full reference](https://github.com/Makio64/gpu-perf-agent/blob/master/docs/reference.md) · [Agent skill](https://github.com/Makio64/gpu-perf-agent/blob/master/skill/SKILL.md)

release.name: repo-07d91b87
release.body:
llama.cpp b11696 with the Gemma 4 / Ministral 3 plain-or-fenced JSON parser fixes and precompiled Metal shaders, identified as b11696-jurilix2.

Upstream source: ceefd16daa2093730bf3340315fa2b84b286ddbc, as for b11696-jurilix1. The patch keeps the b11696-jurilix1 parser fixes and adds two ggml-metal fixes: the macOS 26 target of the tensor kernels replaces the inherited minimum version (otherwise the build fails), and bfloat operations run on the CPU when the library has no bfloat kernels (otherwise a BF16 model aborts at startup). Each receipt identifies the source, patch, parser test logs and every packaged file.

macOS arm64 now ships `default.metallib` (macOS 13.3) and `ggml-tensor.metallib` (macOS 26 tensor API) instead of embedding the shader source, which was compiled at each launch: about 15 s whenever the system Metal cache missed. Built natively on Apple M3 Max: test-chat, test-chat-peg-parser, test-json-schema-to-grammar and test-grammar-parser passed; version identity, minimum macOS 13.3 and all 30 packaged file hashes were verified. In the application's launch cycle the engine started in 3.3–3.6 s each time, against 17.1 s for b11696-jurilix1 when the cache missed. At temperature 0 with product flags, b11696-jurilix1 and this build gave token-identical text and bit-identical embeddings for Gemma 4 12B with MTP and its NER and iter3 adapters, Gemma 4 E4B with MTP and its multitask and iter3 adapters, Qwen3.8 2B with its multitask adapter, Ministral 3 8B with its three adapters, LightOnOCR-2 and EmbeddingGemma. bfloat kernels are no longer available on the GPU; none of the application's models uses BF16 tensors.

Windows CPU, Vulkan and CUDA 12.4 artifacts come from native CI run https://github.com/Makio64/jurilix-llama-runtime/actions/runs/39011677936 (source 089b202), and are attached by the same workflow after receipt, parser-log and archive verification. Windows builds do not compile ggml-metal: only the version identity differs from b11696-jurilix1. CUDA keeps the unchanged upstream b11696 CUDA 12.4 plugin; the CI runner has no NVIDIA driver, so no Windows GPU inference claim is made.
